title.zh: R1 2002 版武器与爆炸物规则
title.en: R1 2002 ED ARMS AND EXPLOSIVES RULES

source.name: Attorney General's Chambers, Brunei Darussalam (AGC) — LAWS OF BRUNEI / Government Gazette

completenessNote: 来源为 AGC 官方 PDF《CAP-58-R1-2002-ED-ARMS-AND-EXPLOSIVES-RULES.pdf》（12 页），本次切分 14 条。该 PDF 为扫描件 + OCR 文本层，正文按版式位置重建：已剔除页眉页脚与边栏条标题、回接折行；未改写措辞、未增删内容。OCR 层面可能存在个别粘连或形近字，逐字引用请以原始 PDF 为准。

text.en: These Rules may be cited as the Arms and Explosives Rules. Firearms to be licensed.

No person shall possess, import or export any gun or arm except under a licence issued by the Licensing Officer: Provided that the provisions of these Rules shall not apply to rifles of a type approved by the Licensing Officer, and ammunition therefor, belonging to any rifle club approved by the Minister and registered or deemed to be registered as a society under the Societies Act (Chapter 66) when stored in any magazine and used on any rifle range approved by the Licensing Officer.

(2) For the purpose of these Rules “Minister” means the Prime Minister.

IMPORTATION AND EXPORTATION Importation of guns and arms.

(1) Any person desiring to import guns or arms shall apply to the Licensing Officer giving a description of the arms, from whom obtained and to whom consigned.

(2) The licence to import shall be in Form 2 in the First Schedule and shall remain in force for a period of 14 days from the date of the arrival of the vessel, vehicle or aircraft in which such guns or arms were imported. Exportation of guns, arms and naval, military and air force stores.

(1) Any person desiring to land or to tranship without landing any guns or arms for the purpose of transhipment on board of any vessel, vehicle or aircraft arriving in Brunei Darussalam shall apply in writing to the Licensing Officer for a permit giving the particulars of the guns or arms. The permit shall be in Form 3 in the First Schedule.

(2) If a permit issued under paragraph (1) is not made use of within 48 hours of the arrival of the vessel, vehicle or aircraft in Brunei Darussalam it shall be returned to the Licensing Officer. Licence to manufacture etc. guns and arms.

Any person desiring to manufacture, deal in, or repair guns or arms shall apply to the Licensing Officer personally or in writing. The licence shall be in Form 4 in the First Schedule and shall terminate on the 30th day of June next following the date of issue. Licence to manufacture, possess etc. explosives.

No person shall manufacture, possess, use, sell, purchase, store, transport, import or export any explosive except under a licence issued by the Licensing Officer. The licence shall be in Form 5 in the First Schedule. Period of validity of explosives licences.
Licences issued under rule 11 shall remain in force for one month only but may be extended at the discretion of the Licensing Officer. Fees.
The fees for licences issued under these Rules shall be as specified in the Second Licensing Officer.

The Minister shall be the Licensing Officer: Provided that the Minister may delegate the exercise of all or any of his powers under these Rules (except this power of delegation) to the Commissioner of Police, but so that no such delegation shall preclude the Minister from exercising at any of the powers so delegated. Restriction on importation of crackers, squibs etc.

No person or persons shall import, manufacture, sell or possess any sand crackers or any squibs or crackers which contain an explosive ingredient or mixture other than black gunpowder (that is to say, sulphur, charcoal and saltpetre) or any squibs or crackers containing more than one-fifth of an ounce by weight of such black gunpowder. Matches not to be sold from premises licensed for explosives.
No matches shall be kept for sale on any premises licensed under rule 11. [S 8/91]

(1) Any person who commits a breach of any of these Rules, other than rule 9, 15 or 16, shall be guilty of an offence and shall be punished with imprisonment for a term of not less than 5 years and not more than 15 years and shall also be punished with whipping with not less than 3 strokes and not more than 12 strokes. [S 11/91]

(2) Any person who commits a breach of rule 9, 15 or 16 shall be guilty of an offence and shall be punished with a fine of $3,000. [S 11/91] Implied conditions in licences.
